intended_object: The set (type) of finite additive subgroups of an additive group A, i.e. {B ≤ A : B finite}. Inferred from the docstring and from its use as the index set of the supremum that defines the supernatural order of a torsion group, `torsionOrder`.
explanation: The definition is the subtype of `AddSubgroup A` made of the subgroups B whose carrier is `Finite`. That is exactly the collection of finite subgroups of A. It only needs an `AddGroup`, which is the natural setting; commutativity is assumed only later, where it is used. There are no degenerate-case problems: the trivial subgroup is always in the collection, and if A is finite then ⊤ is too, which the library uses. Mathlib has no named type of finite subgroups; there it is usually written inline as `{H : AddSubgroup A // Finite H}` or with `Set.Finite`. So this is a faithful formalization of the intended notion.
